messages:
samir: quick sanity check pls — I'm about to apply a TF change that prefers zonal NATs for app subnets and falls back to TGW if NATs are unavailable. worried about brief traffic blackholes during rollout. plan snippet below. pinging @lucy @ben for infra-eyes.

lucy: lgtm overall. careful: AWS route tables use longest-prefix match, not explicit priorities. make the zonal NAT route more-specific if possible (e.g. 10.2.0.0/20) and keep the 0.0.0.0/0 pointing at TGW as fallback.

ben: +1 to lucy. also consider create_before_destroy on the route_table_association and aws_nat_gateway so we don't delete the existing assoc while the new one is still pending.

samir: here's the exact TF resources in the PR:
```hcl
resource "aws_route_table" "app_zonal" {
  vpc_id = var.vpc_id
  tags = { Name = "app-zonal-${var.az}" }
}

resource "aws_route" "to_nat" {
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.app_zonal.id
  destination_cidr_block = var.app_subnet_cidr
  nat_gateway_id         = aws_nat_gateway.zonal.id
}

resource "aws_route" "to_tgw_fallback" {
  route_table_id         = aws_route_table.app_zonal.id
  destination_cidr_block = "0.0.0.0/0"
  transit_gateway_id     = var.tgw_id
}

resource "aws_route_table_association" "assoc" {
  subnet_id      = aws_subnet.app.id
  route_table_id = aws_route_table.app_zonal.id
  lifecycle {
    create_before_destroy = true
  }
}
```

lucy: hmm small nit — destination_cidr_block for to_nat should be the more-specific range used by your service egress, otherwise the 0.0.0.0/0 TGW route will overshadow unless the service IPs are narrower. Also ensure aws_nat_gateway.zonal is created with an EIP that won't be replaced mid-rollout; EIP rotation will kill connections.

ben: if you need zero-downtime, do a canary per-AZ: apply in az-a, verify metrics (tcp resets, error rates), then az-b. we have a terraform var canary_azs or just target the module with `-target=module.egress["az-a"]`.

anika: watch PrivateLink endpoints — if you have interface endpoints in these subnets, route table swaps can briefly affect DNS reachability if you also switch the primary route. Confirm privatelink endpoints are associated to stable subnets, or keep endpoint subnets on a separate route table that doesn't change.

infra-bot: CI: terraform plan OK — no force-replace detected for aws_nat_gateway in this run. (apply blocked pending approvals) :white_check_mark:

samir: perfect — i'll add create_before_destroy to the NAT and keep the endpoint subnets on their own route table. will do canary apply tomorrow morning and post the canary results here. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/3124

lucy: one more thing — add a small smoke test in the canary that probes an external URL through each AZ (two probes: egress via NAT, and fallback via TGW). if the probe fails, auto-rollback.

ben: also tag resources with `egress-canary=true` during the canary for easy cleanup and billing tracking.

samir: thanks all! i'll update the PR with lifecycle rules, smoke probes, and tags. will ping when canary is live. :pray:

anika: cheers — happy to monitor the p99 latency dashboards during the window.

samir: (later) canary went well in az-a — slight increase in tcp retransmits for ~30s, then stable. rolling to az-b in 10m.

ben: :thumbsup:
